memory_candidates.content: Defect class: two independent scans over the same artifact using DIFFERENT match criteria will silently disagree. In this agent system, update-task-status.sh's preflight convenience re-derived the target phase with a narrow `[NOT STARTED]`-only grep, while skill-orchestrate-hard's dispatch loop selected next_phase with a wider `NOT STARTED|IN PROGRESS|PARTIAL|BLOCKED` scan. Whenever the dispatched phase was a resumed/partial one, the narrow scan skipped past it and marked a LATER, undispatched phase [IN PROGRESS] -- which then fed a fabricated CONCURRENT DISPATCH territory-conflict report back into hard-mode reasoning. General rule: any convenience that mutates a per-item marker must take the target item as an explicit parameter from the caller that owns the selection, never independently re-derive it. A second, related trap: a fixture-based regression test for such a side effect passes VACUOUSLY if the fixture omits a dependency the code path early-returns on (here, update-plan-status.sh missing from the fixture copy loop). Every such test needs a positive control asserting the surrounding side effect DID happen.
